newsitem.title: CHINA: McDonalds finally moves disputed Beijing store.
newsitem.headline: McDonalds finally moves disputed Beijing store.

text.p: U.S. fast-food giant McDonald's is to close its flagship China store in the heart of Beijing to make way for a shopping complex after holding out for two years against a removal notice, official media said on Sunday.

The hamburger restaurant, at one end of Beijing's main Wangfujing shopping street and just off central Tiananmen Square, would close on Monday when it would begin its removal, the Beijing Evening News said.

"Following negotiations with relevant departments of the city governent... the McDonald's Development Corp actively supported the alterations to the Wangfujing District of Beijing city and happily accepted the proposal to move," the newspaper said.

McDonald's signed an agreement a few days ago with the Beijing city government to move its flagship restaurant to a temporary site about 150 metres (yards) further north up Wangfujing street, it said.

The restaurant, McDonald's first in China and opened just weeks after the bloody 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown, would be joined by several more along Wangfujing street to meet the development of Beijing's premier shopping road, the newspaper said.

McDonald's had apparently resisted the move on the grounds that it had signed a 20-year lease on the site on prime land in the centre of the capital that will now be developed into a huge commercial and shopping complex by Hong Kong's Cheung Kong (Holdings).
